# Don't Construct Coldness — Evict It

**Intelligent Block:** IB-SMART-NOTE-20261012-sn1105-dont-construct-coldness-evict-it
**Truth state:** CANDIDATE
**Scope:** PRIVATE
**Captured:** 2026-10-12
**Canonical intent:** CAPTURE_DURABLE_INTELLIGENCE
**Provenance:** [t0472] Naya Verity sealed cold-retrieve drill (lesson-broadcast.md, 2026-10-12 ~10:20 PDT; board sign-in 6128606760, Naya Heir Lane 6 t0442 pre-registered drill) — posix_fadvise(DONTNEED) eviction + mincore verification; cold median 1.065s vs warm 0.281s.

> Verified projection of the persisted Intelligent Block. This file is not a second source of truth.

## ✦ IN A NUTSHELL

The t1052 cold-retrieve drill built "cold" test files from fresh inodes — and the creation itself warmed the page cache, proving nothing about cold performance. The method defeated its own measurement before the first read. The t0472 re-run did the opposite: instead of constructing coldness, it **evicted** it — `posix_fadvise(DONTNEED)` on the real retrieve-path files (strace-derived chill set, 607 files), verified evicted with `mincore(2)`, and only then measured. Result: cold median 1.065s vs warm 0.281s, O_DIRECT anchor proven on this filesystem, repo read-only, no drop_caches. A real cold measurement, four times slower than warm — exactly the difference the constructed-coldness test had erased.

The durable rule: **never manufacture the condition you're measuring.** Fresh inodes, new processes, clean temp dirs — every construction step warms what you claim to test cold. The honest method is eviction: take the real path, the real files, the real workload, and remove the warmth (cache eviction, process restart, credential re-entry) — then verify the removal worked (mincore proved the pages were gone) before you measure. And the gate discipline: the drill failed RED on demand before it was allowed to certify GREEN. A gate that never fails is theater (SN-0939); the correct order is prove the gate can bite, then let it pass. Construction-then-measure is the test warming its own testbed. Eviction-then-measure is the truth.

## 🩷 HUMAN NOTE

Shawn — a sharp testing lesson from the cold-retrieve drill: the first drill tried to test "cold" performance by creating fresh test files — but creating files warms the system cache, so the test was never actually cold. It measured warm and called it cold. The redo did it right: take the real files the system actually reads, evict them from cache for real, verify they're actually gone, and only then measure. Cold turned out to be four times slower than warm (1.065s vs 0.281s) — the exact gap the first test had erased by accident. The rule: never build the condition you're trying to measure. Evict it instead, verify the eviction, then measure. And the gate itself had to fail red on demand before anyone trusted its green. A test that warms its own testbed isn't evidence — it's theater with numbers.

## 🟣 CHILD NOTE

Imagine you want to test whether your bike goes fast in the rain — but you only ever test it inside the dry garage! You built a test that skips the very thing you wanted to measure. The smart way: take your real bike, ride it in real rain, and check with your own eyes that it actually got wet first. The lesson: don't build a pretend version of what you're testing. Use the real thing, remove the cheating advantage (dry the road? no — wet it!), and double-check the advantage is really gone before you start the clock. If your test gives itself a head start, the score means nothing.

## 👵 GRANDMA NOTE

Someone wanted to know how slow the computer is when its memory is empty. First try: they made brand-new test files — but making new files fills the memory right back up, so they accidentally tested it full and called it empty. Second try: they took the real files the system actually uses, pushed them out of memory for real, checked that memory was truly empty, and then timed it. It was four times slower — the real answer, hidden by the first test's accident. The lesson: don't build your test so it secretly fixes the thing you're measuring. Empty it for real, verify it's empty, then measure. And make your measuring tool prove it can catch a failure before you trust it when everything looks fine.

## 💜 NAYA NOTE

Note to future me: whenever I design a test of a degraded/cold/empty state, I never construct the state — I evict it. Fresh inodes, fresh processes, clean directories: every construction step warms the testbed and silently converts the measurement into the warm case. The honest sequence: take the REAL path, the REAL files, the REAL workload; remove the warmth (posix_fadvise(DONTNEED) on a strace-derived chill set, verified by mincore(2)); confirm the removal with an independent check before measuring; measure read-only (no drop_caches, no touching the repo). t1052's fresh-inode drill is my permanent example of the failure mode: the creation warmed the cache and proved nothing. And the gate discipline rides with it: fail RED on demand before the gate may certify GREEN (SN-0939). A gate that never bites is theater — prove the bite first, then accept the pass. Construction-then-measure is self-deception; eviction-then-measure is evidence.
